name: Battle of Caporetto

phases.title: The attackers gather east of the Italian line
phases.text: The German and Austro-Hungarian plan sent von Below's army against the Caporetto sector, with Boroević's army attacking the eastern end of the salient and ground near the Adriatic. The Italian Second Army held the line, with the IV and XXVII Corps on either side of the valley.

phases.title: Gas near Bovec
phases.text: In the north, near Bovec, 894 tubes were fired electrically and smothered the Italian trenches in poison gas. The defenders fled, and 500 to 600 of them were killed.

phases.title: Mortars and the guns open fire
phases.text: After a quiet spell, mortars bombarded the Italian wire and trenches at 06:00. At 06:41 2,200 guns opened fire, many aimed at the valley road along which Italian reserves were advancing.

phases.title: The infantry break the line in the valley
phases.text: After two large mines were detonated under strong points on the heights, the infantry attacked and breached the line between the IV and XXVII Corps. Alpine troops went along the ridges on either side to protect the attackers' flanks.

phases.title: The central column drives down the valley road
phases.text: The attackers in the valley marched almost unopposed along the road, and some advanced 25 kilometres on the first day. The Italians beat back the attackers on either side, but the central penetration threw their whole army into disarray.

phases.title: Cadorna orders the retreat
phases.text: Cadorna ordered most of the Italian force to retreat across the Tagliamento, which took four full days. The attackers were close behind.

phases.title: The pursuers ambush the retreating Italians
phases.text: The German and Austro-Hungarian armies were on the heels of the Italians and ambushed the defenders whenever they could.

phases.title: The Italians break through the encirclement
phases.text: The retreating Italian soldiers broke through the Austro-German encirclement and reached the Tagliamento, where the crossing continued.

phases.title: A bridgehead over the Tagliamento
phases.text: After an attack by a battalion of the 4th Bosnian Infantry Regiment, the 55th Infantry Division established a bridgehead across the Tagliamento. The rapid success had stretched German and Austro-Hungarian supply lines to the breaking point.

phases.title: The Italians stand on the Piave
phases.text: The Central Powers could not launch another attack to cut off part of the Italian army against the Adriatic. Cadorna retreated further and by 10 November held a position on the Piave River and Monte Grappa.

note: This plan shows the whole operation of 24 October to 10 November 1917, not a single field: the blocks are armies and corps, and distances are not to scale. The accounts do not say which of the IV and XXVII Corps stood to the north or south of the valley, or where the Italian main force stood before the retreat, so those places are judgement. The two Alpine blocks are placed on the two ridges the accounts name; which ridge lay north is not stated. The Army Group Boroević is shown where it was meant to attack; the accounts do not describe its moves. The 55th Division's bridgehead is placed by judgement along the Tagliamento.
